Celebrating Mark Pilgrim

By: Sophia Phirippides | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
He's been a familiar voice on the radio for almost 3 decades.. charmed us on television with his smile... and inspired many!

Unique Selling Point:
Mark Pilgrim has been a familiar voice on the radio since his first gig at 5fm in 1994. His easy chatter and wit behind the microphone won the hearts of many, but it is his own personal journey that has proved to be an inspiration.

Today, Mark is facing the greatest battle of his life, stage 4 lung cancer that is spreading fast, but it's not the first time he's been faced with a great challenge.

Summary:
At the age of 18 mark was diagnosed with testicular cancer that had spread to his lung and kidneys. He suffered 9 months of gruelling chemo, but emerged a survivor and a changed man. He decided to pursue a career as a radio DJ, but it didn't come easily.

He got a job as consumer researcher to pay the bills, and by night he was a "demo tape" maker, sending countless demos to countless radio stations. After having the door closed in his face for eight years, perseverance eventually paid off when he managed to get his first radio show hosting weekend graveyard on 5FM.

ark spent almost a decade at 5FM hosting various shows, and he's been on many other SA radio stations. His most recent gig was at HOTFM. He also hosted various television programmes and is a well-known public speaker.

Further information:
On 14 July 2008 Mark suffered a sudden and severe heart attack in his doctor's office. Although he suffered permanent heart damage (10% of his heart has lost its functionality), immediate medical intervention saved his life.

And then sadly, in March 2022 the Cancer came back. This time, stage 4 Lung cancer.

Since the end of 2022 he's been in and out of hospital, documenting everything he is going through.

On New Year's Eve Mark surprised South Africans when he proposed marriage to his girlfriend, Adrienne, who had been by his side since his recent diagnosis.

Mark has two daughters from a previous marriage.

Press Release:


After decades thriving through the impact of cancer - embracing life to the full, radio presenter Mark Pilgrim has left us, just at the peak of his broadcasting career. We pay tribute to the bald man with a heart of gold.


Script:


Script:

Intro sequence - Press Button.. Mark Pilgrim Jingle … walk through passages Hot into Studio 1.
Mark: I had a dream, and they always say follow your dream… not going to fall in your lap
Tony: One of the rules in radio is you talk to the listener on a one-on-one basis. And he really did that.
Simon: He'd go on air and he would say “Holy Guacamole”, and I’d sit there and think who says Holy guacamole?
Lloyd: He did
Simon: Mark Pilgrim did.
Jingle/sting
Mark: When I was part of Hot 91.9 - the community station - it wasn't about doing it for a source of income. I was doing it out of a passion for radio. And I think when you put that first, other things come.
Lloyd: Welcome to Studio One here at hot 1027. This was the home of Mark Pilgrim Monday to Saturday from 9 to 12.
Tara: About 14 years ago, I met Mark Pilgrim, as this wet behind-the-ears news anchor - sat down, Good morning, Mr. Pilgrim.And he burst out laughing and said, I'm not Mr. Pilgrim. And I said, It's an honor to meet you. And he said, I've only got one ball. But it made me laugh and it made me feel like I was somewhere I could belong.
VO: I'm Tara Penny of Hot 102.7 FM where Mark Pilgrim found his broadcasting home in the last few years of his extraordinary life. Sadly he lost his final battle with cancer on Sunday the 5th of March. //
Lloyd: He made his journey with cancer public and he wanted to do it for a reason - he said, if I can make a difference of just one person, then I've done my job.
VO: Together with Lloyd Madurai, Simon Parkinson and Tony Murrell we join Carte Blanche and some of his closest colleagues to celebrate Mark Pilgrim - radio legend.
Simon: Even when he was dreadfully sick, that door would close. And that was it. 3 hours of absolute 100% dedication from a presenter who in theory had no problems in the world, even though he did.
VO: Diagnosed with testicular cancer at age 18 he went into depression.
Mark Pilgrim: But I was reading an article on Benjamin Franklin, and he said “some people die at 25 and are only buried at 75”. and I realised that my focus was wrong - I was waiting to die instead of embracing life, but in order to embrace life I had to give myself a goal - my goal was to one day be on radio.
Alex Jay: He was a wonderful colleague across three radio stations. With me. And I worked with the guy for nearly 20 years
VO: Veteran Dj Alex Jay is now with Jacaranda FM
Alex Jay:Pilgrim was quite the trendsetter, he was the first deejay to bring the socials onto the air as part of his content.
Sound up Mark: Today being the 5th of June happy cancer survivors day! And if this applies to you, let me tell you, you are so much more than a survivor, you are a thriver:
Alex Jay: My mom was diagnosed with cancer, also stage four, and she looked up to him as a bit of a hero. She's in remission now. Marky, I wish you were too.
Lloyd:The Mark that everybody heard on the radio was the Mark we knew. He was also a creature of habit - he was incredibly OCD. In fact, I'm looking at the studio now that we're in and he would walk in here and go, Guys.
Tara:He wouldn’t be happy with me having a cuppa.
Lloyd:With this really shouldn't be sitting looking like this.He would place his bag down. He had place for his pen. Everything had a position.
VO: All the way from Texas close friend and fellow broadcaster Darren Scott.
Darren: I always had this suspicion about radio deejays who arrived at work with a banana because as a radio deejay, of course, your healthy eating would be toasted sandwiches, a few burgers and as many beers as possible Mark Pilgrim would arrive at work with a banana. He was the healthiest deejay I knew.
Mark upsound: This is a great cardio exercise.
Simon: when Mark got stage 4 cancer he did say, I'm going to try everything in my power. So he went online, as everyone does. I then started searching for every way, and one of them included
Tara: green juice!
Upsound: Mark: It looks like someone blended Shrek.
Tony: All right let this moment end quickly
Mark: You gotta glug it, and I gotta tell you it's all organic, it cost a fortune so you can't waste it.
Tara: I miss the smell of garlic in the studio.
laugh
Tony: remember when I had to drink that..in the morning his green juice
Upsound: Chug chug…
Mark: Think of it as beer.
Tony: Aargh
Mark: You're only halfway
Tara: What did it taste like?
Tony: Vile

Sound up: Mark dancing with the girls
Lloyd: there were three things that he loved and he loved the most.I mean, his girls to him just meant the world. And Adrian was there for him through everything. And he loved her. all he wanted to do was be on the beach, be with Adrian, have the girls there
And the third thing, he loved was radio.
VO: At the 2022 radio awards Mark won best commercial weekend radio show. Despite being too ill to attend, the reaction by his peers was overwhelming.
Simon: He got a standing ovation .. it went on for ages
Tony: But I think that really did pep him up at the time because that was one of the stages when he was going through a bit of a rough time.
Mark: One of my crucial pillars to health is believing. There are days I'm not well. I acknowledge it, I accept it. But I also know that the next day I will stand up and find something to smile about.
Music montage
Lloyd: All he wanted to do was make an impact, just to one life, he touched millions.
